newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds turned weaker in late trade, ending down after beginning the session stronger, as a variety of factors weighed on prices.

U.S. Treasuries were also lower, while traders noted that the German Bund contract appeared to be led lower by the Conf, falling below 102.10 only after the Swiss Conf contract dipped below 121.60. "Swiss government bonds are expensive relative to swaps," one trader added.
He also said participants may have anticipated a squeeze in Conf futures which did not materialise. "Now it looks like there are too many longs," he added.

In addition, the Swiss government will auction a new federal bond later this month. "Things were going too well," the trader added of the market, which had shown tentative signs of a rebound after last week's selling.

In new issues, BGB Finance launched a 150 million Swiss franc bond, which was led by Bank von Ernst & Cie AG BVEG. The bond, with a 3.00 percent coupon priced at 101.25 maturing April 30, 2004, was quoted in late trade yielding 3.17 percent.
The issue follows other recent offerings for BGB, which include a 150 million sterling deal, a 10 billion yen dual-currency bond, and a 1.5 billion French franc offering.
The lead said it was the first offering in Swiss francs for the borrower.
